topics.t: Writing about a life: relative pronouns
topics.h: 'Bibha was a physicist. She studied cosmic rays.' Two short sentences, or one smooth one? Relative pronouns do the joining!
p: A relative pronoun joins two ideas and refers back to a noun: who, which, whose, whom, that. 'Where' and 'when' can join clauses about places and times.
who = for people: Bibha was a physicist who studied cosmic rays.
which = for things and animals: The star which was named after her is far beyond our Solar System. That can be used for people or things in many sentences.
whose = shows possession: D. M. Bose was the scientist whose laboratory she worked in.
where = for places; when = for times: Kolkata is the city where she was born. 1913 was the year when she was born.

ex.q: Think it through: Join these sentences with a relative pronoun: 'Kalpana Chawla was an astronaut. Her first space flight was in 1997.'
st: The second sentence talks about something that belongs to Kalpana Chawla: 'her first space flight'.
Possession is shown with 'whose'.
Replace 'Her' with 'whose' and join.
ex.a: Kalpana Chawla was an astronaut whose first space flight was in 1997.

topics.rl: Biographies, encyclopedias and school project reports use relative pronouns to pack facts smoothly: 'Kolkata, where she was born, ...'

rv.summary: A relative pronoun joins two ideas and refers back to a noun: who, which, whose, whom, that. 'Where' and 'when' join clauses about places and times.
focus: Join sentences with who, which, whose, where or when.
Use 'whose' for possession.
Pick the right word for people, things, places and times.
remember: who = people; which = things and animals; that = people or things in many sentences.
whose = possession: the scientist whose laboratory she worked in.
where = places; when = times.
traps: Don't use 'which' for a person or 'who' for a thing.
Don't confuse 'whose' with 'who's' (who is).
Don't use 'where' for a time; use 'when'.

qa.q: Read: 'A proud merchant told the court, "I can sell anything, even air!"' Tenali later called this a boast. What does 'boast' mean?
qa.e: A boast is talking proudly about what you can do or have. The merchant proudly claimed he could sell anything.

qa.q: Read: 'The merchant peeped in and said, "But it is empty!" "Exactly," said Tenali, "and so was your boast."' What does Tenali mean?
qa.a: The merchant's claim had nothing real behind it
qa.e: Tenali compares the empty jar to the empty boast: the merchant could not really sell 'anything'.

qa.q: Which phrase is closest in meaning to 'witty'?
qa.e: A witty person says clever things that also make people smile.

qa.q: Tenali Raman's tales are set in the court of which king?
qa.e: Tenali Raman was a poet in the court of Krishnadevaraya of the Vijayanagara Empire.

qa.q: Which of these is the best example of kind wit?
qa.a: A clever joke that makes everyone, even its target, laugh
qa.e: Kind wit makes a point and makes people laugh without hurting anyone.

qa.q: Which word is the opposite of 'foolish'?
qa.e: Foolish means lacking good sense; wise means having good sense. The other words are close to 'foolish', not opposite.

qa.q: In a wit tale, what usually happens right after the hero hears the challenge?
qa.a: The hero thinks of a clever plan
qa.e: The pattern is challenge, then clever plan, then the twist and the laugh at the end.

qa.q: Read: The king sighed, "My cook burnt the rice again. What shall I do, Raman?" Raman bowed. "Make him eat it, Your Majesty. He will never burn it again!" Why is Raman's answer funny?
qa.a: It is an unexpected but clever solution
qa.e: The answer is surprising, yet it makes sense: a cook who has to eat burnt rice will be careful next time.

qa.q: What does the idiom 'to pull someone's leg' mean?
qa.e: It is an idiom, so it is not about a real leg. It means joking with someone by telling them something untrue.

qa.q: 'The comedian had us in stitches.' This means the audience was ___.
qa.e: 'In stitches' means laughing so much that your sides hurt.

qa.q: Which spelling of the noun meaning 'the quality of being funny' is used in British and Indian English?
qa.e: British and Indian English write 'humour'. 'Humor' is the American spelling.

qa.q: Which sentence uses exaggeration to be funny?
qa.a: My school bag weighs a tonne!
qa.e: No school bag weighs a tonne (1000 kg). Saying so is a funny exaggeration, also called hyperbole.

qa.q: What is an idiom?
qa.a: A phrase whose meaning differs from its separate words
qa.e: In an idiom the words together have a special meaning, like 'in stitches' meaning laughing a lot.

qa.q: Meera kept a straight face while Ravi made funny faces. What did Meera do?
qa.e: To keep a straight face is to stop yourself from laughing.

qa.q: Which word is a synonym of 'funny'?
qa.e: Amusing means causing laughter or a smile, which is what funny means. The others are nearly opposites.

qa.q: Choose the correctly spelt adjective formed from 'humour'.
qa.e: Even in British English, the adjective drops the 'u': humorous.

qa.q: Choose the correct reported speech: Ria said, "I am hungry."
qa.a: Ria said that she was hungry.
qa.e: 'I' becomes 'she' and 'am' moves back to 'was' after 'said'.

qa.q: The king asked, "Where are you going, Tenali?" Choose the correct reported speech.
qa.a: The king asked Tenali where he was going.
qa.e: In a reported question the word order becomes like a statement (he was going), and there is no question mark.

qa.q: Mother said to me, "Finish your homework." Choose the correct reported speech.
qa.a: Mother told me to finish my homework.
qa.e: A command is reported with 'told' + person + 'to' + verb.

qa.q: In reported speech after 'said', the word 'tomorrow' usually changes to ___.
qa.e: By the time the words are reported, 'tomorrow' is no longer tomorrow, so it becomes 'the next day'.

qa.q: Arjun asked me, "Can you help me?" Choose the correct reported speech.
qa.a: Arjun asked if I could help him.
qa.e: A yes/no question uses 'asked if'. 'Can' moves back to 'could', 'you' becomes 'I' and 'me' becomes 'him'.

qa.q: Which sentence is in direct speech?
qa.e: Direct speech gives the exact words inside quotation marks.

qa.q: Raju said, "I can solve this riddle." Complete: Raju said that he ___ solve that riddle.
qa.e: After a past reporting verb, 'can' moves back to 'could'.

qa.q: A yes/no question is reported using which word(s)?
qa.e: Yes/no questions are reported with 'if' or 'whether': She asked if I was ready.

qa.q: Read: 'Our cook made parathas so heavy and thick, / Our dog used one as a brand-new brick.' Which two words rhyme?
qa.e: Rhyming words end with the same sound: thick and brick both end in '-ick'.

qa.q: A four-line stanza has lines 1 and 2 rhyming and lines 3 and 4 rhyming. What is its rhyme scheme?
qa.e: The first two lines share sound A, the next two share sound B: AABB.

qa.q: Read: 'Papa took a bite and his jaw went CRACK!' The word 'CRACK' is an example of ___.
qa.e: 'Crack' imitates the sound it names, which is onomatopoeia.

qa.q: Which line uses hyperbole?
qa.a: Our dog used the paratha as a brand-new brick.
qa.e: A paratha cannot really be used as a brick. This deliberate exaggeration is hyperbole.

qa.q: Which line has alliteration?
qa.a: Peter's pet parrot plays the piano.
qa.e: The 'p' sound repeats at the start of Peter's, pet, parrot, plays and piano.

qa.q: What is hyperbole?
qa.e: Hyperbole means exaggerating on purpose, often to be funny or to stress a point.

qa.q: Which word rhymes with 'laugh'?
qa.e: 'Laugh' and 'half' end with the same sound '-af', even though they are spelt differently.

qa.q: In the rhyme scheme ABAB, which lines rhyme?
qa.e: The letter A marks lines 1 and 3; the letter B marks lines 2 and 4. Lines with the same letter rhyme.

qa.q: Which pair are homophones?
qa.e: Flour and flower sound the same but have different spellings and meanings.

qa.q: 'The dog's bark woke me' and 'The tree's bark is rough.' Here 'bark' is a ___.
qa.e: The same word, spelt and said the same way, has two different meanings. That is a homonym.

qa.q: Why is this a pun? 'I tried to be a baker, but I couldn't make enough dough.'
qa.a: 'Dough' means bread mixture and is also slang for money
qa.e: A baker makes dough (the mixture), and 'dough' is also an informal word for money. Both meanings work together.

qa.q: In 'Give me a concrete example', the word 'concrete' means ___.
qa.e: Here 'concrete' is used figuratively to mean definite and real, not the building material.

qa.q: Choose the correct word: The bus was ___ at the red signal.
qa.e: 'Stationary' means not moving. 'Stationery' means paper, pens and other writing materials.

qa.q: Which sentence uses 'right' to mean 'correct'?
qa.e: In 'Your answer is right', right means correct. The others mean a direction, a fair claim, or a side.

qa.q: Which word is a homophone of 'knight'?
qa.e: The 'k' in knight is silent, so knight and night sound the same.

qa.q: Ravi said, 'This maths homework is a piece of cake.' He means it is ___.
qa.e: 'A piece of cake' is an idiom meaning something very easy.

qa.q: Read: Gomti-ma said, "Let one of you divide the mangoes into two heaps, and let the other choose first." Why will the divider make the heaps equal?
qa.a: If one heap is smaller, the other brother will leave it for him
qa.e: The other brother chooses first and will take the bigger heap, so the divider gains nothing by being unfair.

qa.q: What does the phrase 'paves the way' mean in 'Wisdom paves the way'?
qa.e: To pave the way is to prepare a path so something can happen. Wisdom makes a solution possible.

qa.q: What is the adjective form of 'wisdom'?
qa.e: 'Wise' describes a person, so it is the adjective. 'Wisely' is the adverb.

qa.q: Which of these is a proverb?
qa.e: 'Look before you leap' is a short traditional saying that gives advice: think before you act.

qa.q: Folk tales were mostly passed on ___.
qa.e: Folk tales come from times before printing, when people told stories aloud.

qa.q: Which proverb fits? Meena got a small leak in the roof fixed before the monsoon, so the room stayed dry all season.
qa.a: A stitch in time saves nine
qa.e: Fixing a small problem early stopped a bigger one later. That is what 'a stitch in time saves nine' means.

qa.q: What do we call the lesson that a story teaches?
qa.e: The moral is the lesson. The setting is the time and place of the story.

qa.q: Which word is a synonym of 'wise'?
qa.e: A wise person and a sensible person both show good judgement. The other words mean the opposite.

qa.q: Which word shows the LAST step in a sequence?
qa.e: 'Finally' tells the reader that this is the last step.

qa.q: Choose the connector: The well was dry, ___ the villagers dug a new one.
qa.e: The dry well is the reason; digging a new one is the result. 'So' introduces a result.

qa.q: Which sentence shows cause and effect?
qa.a: It rained heavily, so the match was called off.
qa.e: Heavy rain (cause) led to the match being called off (effect), joined by 'so'.

qa.q: What should you do FIRST when solving a problem?
qa.e: You cannot choose a good solution until you understand the problem.

qa.q: 'Although the path was steep, the children kept climbing.' The word 'although' shows ___.
qa.e: 'Although' shows something surprising: the path was hard, yet they kept going.

qa.q: Pick the best order: (a) Water the seed (b) Dig a small hole (c) Put the seed in (d) Cover it with soil
qa.e: You dig the hole, place the seed, cover it with soil and then water it.

qa.q: In a sentence, the connector 'because' introduces ___.
qa.e: 'Because' answers 'why?': We stayed in because it rained.

qa.q: Choose the best connector: 'Ravi missed the bus. ___, he was late for school.'
qa.e: Being late is the result of missing the bus, so 'As a result' fits.

qa.q: 'Don't give up, you are close to the answer!' Here 'give up' means ___.
qa.e: 'Give up' means to stop trying.

qa.q: Choose the phrasal verb: Meera ___ a smart way to share the mangoes.
qa.e: 'Came up with' means thought of an idea. 'Came down with' means fell ill.

qa.q: Which phrasal verb means 'to investigate'?
qa.e: To look into something is to examine it carefully. 'Look up to' means to respect someone.

qa.q: 'The school trip was put off because of the rain.' Here 'put off' means ___.
qa.e: 'Put off' means moved to a later time, which is postponed.

qa.q: Which sentence means 'We had no milk left'?
qa.e: To run out of something is to use it all up so none is left.

qa.q: 'Please look after my tulsi plant while I am away.' Here 'look after' means ___.
qa.e: To look after something is to take care of it.

qa.q: Which of these means 'to hand out for free'?
qa.e: 'Give away' means to give something for free. 'Give up' is stop trying; 'give in' is accept defeat.

qa.q: A phrasal verb is made of ___.
qa.a: a verb plus a particle such as up, out or into
qa.e: Examples: give + up, look + into, run + out of. The words together carry a new meaning.

qa.q: The Param Vir Chakra is ___.
qa.a: India's highest military award for gallantry
qa.e: The PVC is the highest gallantry award of India's armed forces, for bravery in the face of the enemy.

qa.q: Who was the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra?
qa.e: Major Somnath Sharma was the first. Captain Vikram Batra also received the PVC, but in 1999.

qa.q: The Battle of Badgam was fought on ___.
qa.e: The battle took place on 3 November 1947, a few months after Independence.

qa.q: 'He was awarded the medal posthumously.' Here 'posthumously' means ___.
qa.e: 'Posthumous' means happening after a person's death.

qa.q: Major Somnath Sharma belonged to which regiment?
qa.e: He was an officer of the 4th Battalion of the Kumaon Regiment (4 Kumaon).

qa.q: Read: 'Though his arm was in plaster, he moved from post to post, cheering his men.' What does this tell us?
qa.a: He was injured but still led his men bravely
qa.e: 'Though' shows contrast: even with an injured arm, he kept leading and encouraging his soldiers.

qa.q: Badgam is in which present-day Union Territory of India?
qa.e: Badgam (also spelt Budgam) is near Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir.

qa.q: Which word means 'great courage, especially in battle'?
qa.e: 'Valour' means great bravery, as in the chapter title 'A Tale of Valour'.

qa.q: Which word is a synonym of 'courage'?
qa.e: Bravery and courage both mean facing danger or difficulty without giving in to fear.

qa.q: Which word is the antonym of 'brave'?
qa.e: Cowardly means lacking courage, the opposite of brave. The other words are synonyms.

qa.q: What is the abstract noun formed from 'strong'?
qa.e: Strong (adjective) → strength (abstract noun). 'Strongly' is an adverb and 'stronger' is a comparative.

qa.q: Which of these is an abstract noun?
qa.e: Honesty is a quality that cannot be seen or touched. The others are things or people you can see.

qa.q: Choose the correct word: The firefighter was praised for his ___.
qa.e: After 'his' we need a noun, and the noun form is 'bravery'.

qa.q: What does 'gallantry' mean in 'an award for gallantry'?
qa.e: Gallantry awards honour great bravery, especially in battle or danger.

qa.q: Which sentence shows everyday courage?
qa.a: Asha told the truth even though she feared being scolded.
qa.e: Telling the truth when you are afraid of the result takes courage.

qa.q: What is the abstract noun formed from 'hero'?
qa.e: Heroism is the quality of being a hero. 'Heroic' is an adjective and 'heroes' is a plural.

qa.q: Which sentence is in the past continuous tense?
qa.e: Was + writing (verb-ing) shows an action in progress in the past.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: The film ___ when we reached the hall.
qa.e: The film started before we reached, so the earlier action takes the past perfect 'had started'.

qa.q: What is the past tense of 'lead'?
qa.e: 'Lead' is irregular: lead-led-led.

qa.q: 'They were digging the garden when the rain began.' Which action was already in progress?
qa.e: 'Were digging' is past continuous, a longer action that the rain interrupted.

qa.q: Which tense shows an action completed before another past action?
qa.e: The past perfect (had + past participle) marks the earlier of two past actions.

qa.q: Fill in the blank: Yesterday, the students ___ the national flag at dawn.
qa.e: 'Yesterday' is a definite past time, so the simple past 'hoisted' is correct.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: While I ___ my homework, the lights went off.
qa.e: Homework was in progress when a shorter action interrupted it, so use past continuous.

qa.q: What is the past participle of 'give'?
qa.e: give-gave-given. 'Gave' is the simple past; 'given' is the past participle, used with 'had' or 'has'.

qa.q: Read: 'The bus was full, the seats were gone, / An old man held the rail alone.' Why was the old man holding the rail?
qa.a: There was no seat for him
qa.e: The first line says the seats were gone, so he had to stand and hold the rail.

qa.q: Read: 'A thank-you bloomed upon his face.' This line is a ___.
qa.e: It compares his growing smile to a flower blooming, without 'like' or 'as'. That is a metaphor.

qa.q: Read: '"He's someone's grandpa, just like mine," she thought.' What feeling made the girl help?
qa.e: She imagined the old man as her own grandfather. Imagining another's feelings is empathy.

qa.q: Which line is an example of personification?
qa.a: The old bus groaned up the hill.
qa.e: Groaning is a human action given to the bus. 'As slow as a snail' is a simile.

qa.q: What is the theme of a poem?
qa.e: The theme is the central idea, such as kindness to elders.

qa.q: Which word is the antonym of 'kind'?
qa.e: Cruel means causing pain or not caring, which is opposite to kind.

qa.q: Which word best describes an elderly person who is weak and delicate?
qa.e: 'Frail' means physically weak and delicate.

qa.q: A group of lines in a poem is called a ___.
qa.e: A stanza is to a poem what a paragraph is to prose.

qa.q: Which request is the most polite?
qa.a: Could you please pass me the remote?
qa.e: 'Could you please...' is a polite request form.

qa.q: Which modal is used for asking permission formally?
qa.e: 'May I...?' is the formal, polite way to ask permission.

qa.q: 'Shall I bring you a glass of water, Nani?' The speaker is ___.
qa.e: 'Shall I...?' is used to offer to do something for someone.

qa.q: Which modal gives advice?
qa.e: 'You should rest' gives advice. 'Can' shows ability or informal permission.

qa.q: 'When Dadaji was young, he ___ climb coconut trees.' Choose the modal for past ability.
qa.e: 'Could' is the past form of 'can' and shows ability in the past.

qa.q: Which sentence shows respect to an elder?
qa.a: Let me hold your hand while we cross, Nanaji.
qa.e: Offering a hand gently is caring and respectful. The others are impatient or rude.

qa.q: Which modal shows a rule in this museum sign? 'Visitors ___ not touch the paintings.'
qa.e: A rule or strong necessity uses 'must'. 'Must not' means it is not allowed.

qa.q: Which word is a synonym of 'respect'?
qa.e: To honour someone is to show them great respect.

qa.q: Who is known as the 'Father of the White Revolution' in India?
qa.e: Verghese Kurien led India's dairy revolution. M. S. Swaminathan is linked with the Green Revolution.

qa.q: The White Revolution is linked with a big increase in the production of ___.
qa.e: 'White' stands for milk. Fish is the Blue Revolution and wheat is linked with the Green Revolution.

qa.q: When is National Milk Day celebrated in India?
qa.e: It is celebrated on 26 November, Verghese Kurien's birthday. (1 June is World Milk Day.)

qa.q: In which state was Verghese Kurien born?
qa.e: He was born in Kozhikode, Kerala, though his life's work was in Anand, Gujarat.

qa.q: Operation Flood was launched in which year?
qa.e: The NDDB launched Operation Flood in 1970.

qa.q: Read: 'Kurien was an engineer, not a farmer. Yet he decided to stay and help the farmers of Anand.' The word 'Yet' shows ___.
qa.e: 'Yet' means 'but still'. It contrasts his engineering training with his choice to work with farmers.

qa.q: What is the title of Verghese Kurien's memoir?
qa.e: His memoir is 'I Too Had a Dream'. 'Wings of Fire' is by A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

qa.q: Which word means 'to become successful and well-off'?
qa.e: To prosper is to do well and grow richer. Kurien wanted farmers to prosper.

qa.q: What is a cooperative?
qa.a: A group owned and run by its members for their shared benefit
qa.e: In a cooperative, the members are the owners and share the benefits.

qa.q: The Kaira District Cooperative Milk Producers' Union was formed in 1946 in which town?
qa.e: The union was formed at Anand in Kaira (Kheda) district, Gujarat.

qa.q: Which farmers' leader led the Kaira union at Anand?
qa.e: Tribhuvandas Patel led the farmers' union and persuaded Kurien to stay on and help it.

qa.q: In the Anand pattern, who collects milk directly from the farmers?
qa.e: The village society is the first level. It collects and tests the milk from member farmers.

qa.q: Read: 'At the end of the year, Lakshmiben also gets a share of the profit, because she is a member.' Why does she get a share?
qa.a: She is a member of the cooperative
qa.e: The passage says she gets a share because she is a member. Members share the profits.

qa.q: How does a cooperative help farmers get a fairer price?
qa.e: Members sell through their own system, so the money does not go to middlemen.

qa.q: The prefix 'co-' in 'cooperative' means ___.
qa.e: 'Co-' means together, as in co-operate (work together), co-author and co-pilot.

qa.q: Which of these is a cooperative?
qa.a: A housing society run by its residents
qa.e: A housing society is owned and managed by its member residents.

qa.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
qa.a: Milk is sold by the farmer.
qa.e: 'Is sold' (be + past participle) with the receiver 'milk' as subject is passive.

qa.q: Change to passive: 'The society tests the milk.'
qa.a: The milk is tested by the society.
qa.e: Present tense 'tests' becomes 'is tested', and the object 'the milk' becomes the subject.

qa.q: Change to passive: 'Kurien wrote a memoir.'
qa.a: A memoir was written by Kurien.
qa.e: Simple past 'wrote' becomes 'was written', using the past participle 'written'.

qa.q: Complete in the passive: 'The milk ___ to Mumbai tomorrow.'
qa.e: 'Tomorrow' is future, and passive future is will be + past participle.

qa.q: In 'The cheese was made by the cooperative', who did the action?
qa.e: In a passive sentence, the doer comes after 'by'.

qa.q: Why is the passive often used to describe a process?
qa.a: The steps matter more than who does them
qa.e: In processes, what happens to the milk matters more than which worker does it.

qa.q: Change to active: 'The calves are fed by Raju.'
qa.e: The doer 'Raju' becomes the subject, and present passive 'are fed' becomes present active 'feeds'.

qa.q: Choose the correct passive form: 'The milk ___ right now.'
qa.e: 'Right now' needs the present continuous; in the passive that is is being + past participle.

qa.q: Read: 'Grandma said, "I was at the market all evening," and the shopkeeper agreed.' What does Grandma have?
qa.e: An alibi is proof that a person was somewhere else when the event happened. The shopkeeper confirms it.

qa.q: Read: 'Kavya pointed at the cat, but the fridge door was too heavy for a cat to open.' The cat is a ___.
qa.e: The cat is a false lead that cannot be true, which makes it a red herring.

qa.q: What is a 'motive'?
qa.e: The motive is why someone did it, for example, loving sweets.

qa.q: Which of these is evidence?
qa.a: Syrup stains on Ravi's homework book
qa.e: Evidence is a real fact or object. Guesses, feelings and rumours are not evidence.

qa.q: What usually happens at the end of a mystery story?
qa.a: The solution is revealed and explained
qa.e: Mysteries end with the reveal, when the detective explains how the clues lead to the answer.

qa.q: The person who actually committed the wrongdoing is the ___.
qa.e: The culprit is the one who really did it. A suspect only might have done it.

qa.q: Which word means 'to work out a conclusion from clues'?
qa.e: To deduce is to reach a conclusion by reasoning. Detectives deduce from clues.

qa.q: Which Indian writer created the detective Feluda?
qa.e: Satyajit Ray, the famous filmmaker, also wrote the Feluda detective stories.

qa.q: All the students of Class 8B wore white on Friday. Neha is in Class 8B. What can we deduce?
qa.e: If all of 8B wore white and Neha is in 8B, then Neha wore white. Nothing tells us what she likes.

qa.q: Read: 'Arjun came in with muddy shoes and a wet umbrella.' What can you infer?
qa.e: A wet umbrella and mud are clues that point to rain.

qa.q: Which of these is a fact rather than an inference?
qa.e: What a clock shows can be checked directly, so it is a fact. The others are conclusions.

qa.q: Read the first letter of each word to find the hidden word: 'Every Xylophone Is Totally Silent.'
qa.e: E-X-I-T-S spells EXITS.

qa.q: Some birds in Ravi's garden are parrots. Mithu is a bird in Ravi's garden. What can we say for sure?
qa.a: We cannot be sure whether Mithu is a parrot
qa.e: 'Some' does not mean 'all', so Mithu may or may not be a parrot.

qa.q: What is an inference?
qa.a: A conclusion from clues and what you already know
qa.e: An inference uses evidence and knowledge to reach a sensible conclusion.

qa.q: Read: 'The shop opens only on weekdays.' Today is Sunday. What can we deduce?
qa.e: Sunday is not a weekday, and the shop opens only on weekdays, so it is closed.

qa.q: Read: 'The lights in Meena's room were off, her bag was gone and her shoes were missing from the rack.' The best inference is that Meena ___.
qa.e: Her bag and shoes are gone and her room is dark, so she has probably gone out.

qa.q: 'The streets are wet and people are carrying umbrellas. It ___ have rained.'
qa.e: The clues make it almost certain, so we use 'must have'.

qa.q: Which modal shows that something is possible but not certain?
qa.e: 'Might' (and may/could) shows possibility.

qa.q: 'That ___ be Rohan's bicycle; his is red and this one is blue.'
qa.e: The colours do not match, so it is almost certainly not his: can't.

qa.q: Choose the correct past deduction.
qa.e: The pattern is modal + have + past participle: must have forgotten.

qa.q: 'He might be at the library.' How sure is the speaker?
qa.e: 'Might' shows the speaker thinks it is possible but is not sure.

qa.q: The detective said, 'The thief must have climbed the wall.' This means the detective is ___.
qa.e: 'Must have' shows a strong, almost certain deduction about the past.

qa.q: Which sentence uses a modal of deduction?
qa.a: You must be Riya's brother; you look just like her!
qa.e: Here 'must' means 'I am almost sure' (a deduction). In the others, 'must' gives a rule or duty.

qa.q: 'Mummy isn't answering the phone. She ___ be driving.' Choose the best modal for a possibility.
qa.e: 'Could' shows one possible reason, which fits when we are not sure.

qa.q: Which of these is a fantasy element?
qa.a: A painted bird flies off the paper
qa.e: A painted bird cannot really fly, so it is fantasy. The others can happen in real life.

qa.q: Read: 'Whatever Kabir painted for others came alive, but nothing he painted for himself ever moved.' What does this suggest about the magic?
qa.a: It works only when used to help others
qa.e: The magic works for others, not for himself, so it rewards helping others.

qa.q: In a plot, the turning point of greatest tension is called the ___.
qa.e: The climax is the turning point, after which the story moves towards its end.

qa.q: Who is the protagonist of a story?
qa.e: The protagonist is the central character. In Kabir's tale it is Kabir.

qa.q: Read: 'A greedy trader demanded a painted mountain of gold, but Kabir refused.' Why did Kabir refuse?
qa.a: He did not want to use his gift for greed
qa.e: Kabir uses his gift to help, so he refuses a greedy demand. He paints for the children instead.

qa.q: Which part of the plot introduces the characters and the setting?
qa.e: The exposition comes first and sets up who, where and when.

qa.q: What is the setting of Kabir's tale?
qa.e: The tale opens in a dry village of Bundelkhand, so that is its setting.

qa.q: Which word means 'the power to form pictures and ideas in the mind'?
qa.e: Imagination is the ability to picture things that are not in front of you.

qa.q: What is the noun form of 'just'?
qa.e: Just (adjective) → justice (noun). 'Justly' is an adverb and 'justify' is a verb.

qa.q: Which is the correct opposite of 'legal'?
qa.e: Words beginning with 'l' usually take il-: illegal, illogical.

qa.q: Which is the correct opposite of 'responsible'?
qa.e: Words beginning with 'r' usually take ir-: irresponsible, irregular.

qa.q: Madhubani painting comes from which state?
qa.e: Madhubani (Mithila) painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar.

qa.q: Warli painting, with its simple circles and triangles, comes from which state?
qa.e: Warli art is made by the Warli community of Maharashtra.

qa.q: Which word is the opposite of 'justice'?
qa.e: The opposite noun is 'injustice'. 'Unjust' is the opposite adjective.

qa.q: Which prefix makes the opposite of 'honest'?
qa.e: The opposite of honest is dishonest.

qa.q: Which sentence shows justice in a story?
qa.a: The honest weaver is finally paid fairly for her work.
qa.e: Justice means fairness: the honest weaver gets what she deserves.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: Kabir's painting is ___ than Ravi's.
qa.e: 'Than' compares two things, so we use the comparative 'brighter'. 'More brighter' doubles the comparison.

qa.q: What is the superlative of 'good'?
qa.e: 'Good' is irregular: good-better-best.

qa.q: Which is correct?
qa.e: Long adjectives form the superlative with 'the most'.

qa.q: What is the comparative of 'bad'?
qa.e: 'Bad' is irregular: bad-worse-worst. 'Worse' compares two things.

qa.q: Choose the correct spelling of the superlative of 'happy'.
qa.e: Change -y to -i and add -est: happiest.

qa.q: Which sentence uses the comparative degree?
qa.a: Asha's drawing is neater than mine.
qa.e: 'Neater than' compares two drawings. 'The neatest' is superlative.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'Of the three brothers, Raju is the ___.'
qa.e: With three or more, use the superlative: the tallest.

qa.q: What is the comparative of 'big'?
qa.e: After a single short vowel, double the last consonant: big → bigger.

qa.q: Living root bridges are found in which state?
qa.e: They are found in Meghalaya, grown by the Khasi and Jaintia communities.

qa.q: What are 'phumdis' on Loktak Lake?
qa.a: Floating masses of plants and soil
qa.e: Phumdis are floating mats of vegetation and soil, some large enough to carry a national park.

qa.q: Which animal is the famous resident of Keibul Lamjao National Park?
qa.e: The sangai, a deer, lives on the floating phumdis of Loktak Lake.

qa.q: How was Lonar Lake in Maharashtra formed?
qa.a: By a meteorite striking the Earth
qa.e: Lonar Lake fills a crater made by a meteorite impact.

qa.q: Read: 'At Bhedaghat, the Narmada slips between cliffs of white marble.' Which river is described?
qa.e: The sentence names the Narmada, which flows past the Marble Rocks.

qa.q: The Sundarbans is best known for its ___.
qa.a: mangrove forests and Royal Bengal tigers
qa.e: The Sundarbans delta has huge mangrove forests and is home to the Royal Bengal tiger.

qa.q: Which wonder is a vast white salt desert in Gujarat?
qa.e: The Great Rann of Kutch is a huge salt desert in Gujarat.

qa.q: Which word means 'amazing to look at'?
qa.e: 'Spectacular' means wonderful and striking to see, as in 'Spectacular Wonders'.

qa.q: Which sentence is the most descriptive?
qa.a: Silver waves rushed over the warm, golden sand.
qa.e: It uses colour, movement and touch (silver, rushed, warm, golden), so the reader can picture it.

qa.q: Which detail appeals to the sense of smell?
qa.e: Fragrance is a smell. The others are about sight, touch and sound.

qa.q: Read: 'The lake was a mirror for the sky.' This is a ___.
qa.e: It compares the lake to a mirror directly, without 'like' or 'as'.

qa.q: Which sentence 'shows' instead of 'tells' that it was cold?
qa.a: Our breath made little clouds, and our fingers went numb.
qa.e: It lets the reader feel the cold through details, without just saying 'cold'.

qa.q: Which word is a more vivid choice than 'walked slowly'?
qa.e: 'Strolled' paints a picture of walking slowly and calmly.

qa.q: Read: 'The wind whistled through the valley.' Which sense does this detail appeal to?
qa.e: 'Whistled' is something you hear.

qa.q: Which is a good way to organise a description of a waterfall?
qa.a: From the top of the falls down to the pool
qa.e: Describing top to bottom (or near to far) helps the reader follow the picture.

qa.q: Which adjective best replaces 'very big' in 'a very big mountain'?
qa.e: 'Massive' means very large and solid.

qa.q: Choose the correct preposition: The tiger swam ___ the river to the other bank.
qa.e: Going from one side to the other side of a river is 'across'.

qa.q: Choose the correct preposition: The road goes ___ a thick forest.
qa.e: A road inside a forest, from one end to the other, goes through it.

qa.q: Which sentence uses 'besides' correctly?
qa.e: 'Besides' means 'in addition to'. For 'next to', use 'beside'.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: The frog jumped ___ the pond.
qa.e: 'Into' shows movement from outside to inside.

qa.q: Divide the laddoos ___ the two sisters.
qa.e: With two people, use 'between'. Use 'among' for more than two.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: We walked ___ the bank of the Brahmaputra.
qa.e: Walking following the length of a river bank is 'along'.

qa.q: What does a preposition show?
qa.a: The relation of a noun to other words, such as place or direction
qa.e: Prepositions like on, across and through link a noun or pronoun to the rest of the sentence.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: The cat climbed ___ the roof.
qa.e: 'Onto' shows movement to a position on top of a surface.

qa.q: Who wrote 'The Cherry Tree'?
qa.e: 'The Cherry Tree' is by Ruskin Bond, who writes about life in the hills.

qa.q: Where does Ruskin Bond live?
qa.e: He has lived for many years in Landour, Mussoorie, in Uttarakhand.

qa.q: Which of these is a book by Ruskin Bond?
qa.e: 'The Blue Umbrella' is by Ruskin Bond. 'Malgudi Days' is by R. K. Narayan.

qa.q: Read: 'For weeks nothing happened. She almost forgot it.' What quality did Tara need?
qa.e: Waiting for weeks without results needs patience.

qa.q: Read: 'Then one rainy morning she spotted two tiny green leaves pushing up through the earth.' What had happened to the apricot stone?
qa.e: Two tiny leaves pushing up means the seed had sprouted (germinated).

qa.q: Ruskin Bond was born in which state?
qa.e: He was born in Kasauli, which is in Himachal Pradesh.

qa.q: What do Ruskin Bond's stories mostly celebrate?
qa.e: His stories are full of hills, trees, birds and ordinary people.

qa.q: Which award did 'Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra' win?
qa.e: It won the Sahitya Akademi Award, an important Indian literary prize.

qa.q: What is a sapling?
qa.e: A sapling is a young tree, older than a seedling.

qa.q: Which comes first in a plant's life?
qa.e: A plant's life begins with a seed.

qa.q: 'Without water, the plant began to ___.' Choose the best word.
qa.e: Plants without water dry up and shrink: they wither.

qa.q: What is the opposite of 'patience'?
qa.e: Patience → impatience (with the prefix im- before p).

qa.q: Choose the adverb: 'She waited ___ for the seed to sprout.'
qa.e: 'Waited' is a verb, and an adverb describes how she waited: patiently.

qa.q: What does 'germinate' mean?
qa.e: A seed germinates when it starts to grow and sends out a shoot.

qa.q: Which proverb is about patience?
qa.a: Rome was not built in a day.
qa.e: It means big things take time, so we must be patient.

qa.q: Which word is a synonym of 'perseverance'?
qa.e: Perseverance means continuing to try with determination.

qa.q: Which sentence is in the present perfect tense?
qa.e: Has + past participle (grown) makes the present perfect.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'I have lived here ___ 2019.'
qa.e: 2019 is a point in time, so use 'since'.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'She has practised the sitar ___ two hours.'
qa.e: Two hours is a length of time, so use 'for'.

qa.q: Which sentence is correct?
qa.a: I saw the cherry blossoms yesterday.
qa.e: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so use the simple past 'saw'.

qa.q: Complete: 'They ___ just finished planting the saplings.'
qa.e: 'They' takes 'have': They have just finished.

qa.q: Which sentence uses the present perfect continuous?
qa.a: It has been raining since morning.
qa.e: Has been + raining shows an action that started earlier and is still going on.

qa.q: What is the past participle of 'grow'?
qa.e: grow-grew-grown. The present perfect uses 'grown': has grown.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'Our neighbour ___ looked after the garden since last winter.'
qa.e: 'Since last winter' needs the present perfect, and the singular subject takes 'has'.

qa.q: Read: 'Golden fields bow low to greet the sun.' Which figure of speech is used?
qa.e: Fields are given the human actions of bowing and greeting.

qa.q: What is a hymn?
qa.e: A hymn is a song of praise or thanks.

qa.q: Read: 'The sickles sing: the reaping has begun!' What does 'reaping' mean?
qa.e: To reap is to cut and gather a crop. Sickles are the tools used for it.

qa.q: Read: 'Rain gave its silver, soil gave its might.' What does 'silver' stand for here?
qa.e: The poet uses 'silver' to describe shining drops of rain that helped the crops.

qa.q: Pongal is a harvest festival of which state?
qa.e: Pongal is celebrated in Tamil Nadu, when the new rice is cooked.

qa.q: Which word best describes the tone of a harvest hymn?
qa.e: Harvest hymns give thanks, so the tone is grateful and joyful.

qa.q: Bihu, celebrated with dance and music, is a festival of which state?
qa.e: Bihu is celebrated in Assam.

qa.q: Read the last two lines: 'Rain gave its silver, soil gave its might, / Now every grain glows warm and bright.' Which two words rhyme?
qa.e: 'Might' and 'bright' end with the same '-ight' sound.

qa.q: Which of these is a rabi crop?
qa.e: Wheat is sown in winter and harvested in spring, so it is a rabi crop.

qa.q: Kharif crops are sown at the start of which season?
qa.e: Kharif crops need lots of water, so they are sown when the monsoon begins.

qa.q: What does 'threshing' mean?
qa.e: Threshing separates the grain from the harvested stalks.

qa.q: Which step comes right after sowing?
qa.e: Seeds need water to grow, so irrigation comes after sowing.

qa.q: Choose the correct collective noun: 'a ___ of cattle'.
qa.e: A group of cattle is a herd. A flock is used for birds or sheep.

qa.q: Choose the correct collective noun: 'a ___ of wheat'.
qa.e: A bundle of cut wheat stalks tied together is a sheaf.

qa.q: Read: 'Ramesh sows seeds in June when the rains start, and harvests in October.' What type of crop is this?
qa.e: June sowing with the monsoon and October harvest is the kharif pattern.

qa.q: What is the meaning of 'irrigation'?
qa.e: Irrigation means watering fields through canals, wells, pipes or sprinklers.

qa.q: Read: 'Every evening, Baba stood at the edge of the cracked field and studied the sky.' Why was the field cracked?
qa.a: It had not rained for a long time
qa.e: Soil cracks when it dries out, which happens when there is no rain for a long time.

qa.q: Read: 'A cool wind rattled the tin roof, and the smell of wet earth drifted in.' What do these details suggest?
qa.e: A cool wind and the smell of wet earth are signs of rain.

qa.q: Which state does the south-west monsoon usually reach first?
qa.e: The south-west monsoon usually reaches Kerala first, around 1 June.

qa.q: What is a drought?
qa.a: A long period with too little rain
qa.e: In a drought, rain is too little for a long time, so crops and people suffer.

qa.q: What does 'petrichor' mean?
qa.a: The earthy smell when rain falls on dry ground
qa.e: Petrichor is the pleasant earthy smell of rain on dry soil.

qa.q: Rainfall is measured with a ___.
qa.e: A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall, usually in millimetres.

qa.q: Which word means 'light, fine rain'?
qa.e: A drizzle is light rain with tiny drops.

qa.q: Read: 'Baba smiled for the first time in weeks.' What does this tell us about Baba's feelings before?
qa.a: He had been worried for weeks
qa.e: 'For the first time in weeks' shows he had not smiled because he was worried about the rain.

qa.q: Which word is an antonym of 'hope'?
qa.e: Despair means having no hope at all. The others are close to hope in meaning.

qa.q: The suffix '-less' in 'hopeless' means ___.
qa.e: -less means without: hopeless means without hope.

qa.q: Read: 'Many neighbours sold their bullocks. But Amma still cleaned the seed sacks every morning.' What does 'But' show?
qa.a: Amma acted differently from the neighbours
qa.e: 'But' shows contrast: unlike the neighbours, Amma kept preparing.

qa.q: What does 'every cloud has a silver lining' mean?
qa.a: Something good can come out of a bad situation
qa.e: The idiom means even bad times can bring something good.

qa.q: Choose the correct word: 'We are ___ that the rain will come soon.'
qa.e: After 'are', we need an adjective that means full of hope: hopeful.

qa.q: Which word means 'unable to rest or keep still'?
qa.e: -less means without, so restless means without rest.

qa.q: 'There is light at the end of the tunnel' means ___.
qa.a: A difficult time is coming to an end
qa.e: The idiom means the end of a hard time is in sight.

qa.q: Which sentence shows hope?
qa.a: I am sure tomorrow will be better.
qa.e: Believing that tomorrow will be better is hope. The others show despair.

qa.q: Which sentence is a prediction based on what we can see now?
qa.a: Look out! That glass is going to fall.
qa.e: We can see the glass about to fall, so we use 'going to'.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'Your bag looks heavy. I ___ carry it for you.'
qa.e: This is a quick offer made at the moment of speaking, so 'will' + base verb fits.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'We ___ sow the seeds next week; we have already bought them.'
qa.e: This is a plan already made, so 'are going to' is the best choice.

qa.q: Which sentence uses 'hope' correctly?
qa.e: Rain tomorrow is possible, so 'hope' with a present verb is correct.

qa.q: Which sentence uses 'wish' correctly for something impossible?
qa.a: I wish I could breathe underwater.
qa.e: 'Wish' + could shows an impossible or unreal situation.

qa.q: Which sentence uses 'will' correctly?
qa.a: She will go to the market.
qa.e: 'Will' is followed by the base form of the verb: will go.

qa.q: 'We are leaving for Ooty on Saturday.' What does the present continuous show here?
qa.e: With a future time (on Saturday), the present continuous shows a planned arrangement.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'The weather office says it ___ rain heavily in Chennai tomorrow.'
qa.e: Weather forecasts often use 'will' for predictions.

qa.q: Who wrote 'Feathered Friend'?
qa.e: 'Feathered Friend' is a science fiction story by Arthur C. Clarke.

qa.q: What does the title 'Feathered Friend' refer to?
qa.e: 'Feathered' means having feathers, so a feathered friend is a bird.

qa.q: Why did miners take canaries into coal mines?
qa.a: As an early warning of dangerous gases
qa.e: Canaries react to harmful gases sooner than people, so they warned miners of danger.

qa.q: Arthur C. Clarke lived for many years in which country?
qa.e: He moved to Sri Lanka in 1956 and lived there until 2008.

qa.q: Read: 'One morning every plant was drooping, though he had watered them the night before.' Why was the drooping surprising?
qa.a: He had watered them, so they should have been fine
qa.e: 'Though he had watered them' shows that drooping was not expected.

qa.q: How often does the International Space Station go around the Earth?
qa.e: It travels very fast and goes around the Earth roughly every 90 minutes.

qa.q: Why must air be recycled on a space station?
qa.a: Space has no air to breathe
qa.e: There is no breathable air in space, so a station must carry, make and recycle its own.

qa.q: Which gas, dangerous in coal mines, were canaries used to detect?
qa.e: Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas with no smell. Canaries showed its effects first.

qa.q: What is science fiction?
qa.a: Imaginative stories based on science and technology
qa.e: Sci-fi imagines new worlds or futures using science and technology.

qa.q: Which of these is most likely science fiction?
qa.a: A boy builds a robot that recycles plastic into toys
qa.e: The robot is based on technology. The others use magic or talking animals.

qa.q: Who was the first Indian to travel to space?
qa.e: Rakesh Sharma flew to space in 1984. Kalpana Chawla flew later, in 1997.

qa.q: Which mission landed near the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023?
qa.e: Chandrayaan-3's lander touched down near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023.

qa.q: Which character is an inventor in Satyajit Ray's science fiction stories?
qa.e: Professor Shonku is Ray's inventor-scientist. Feluda is his detective.

qa.q: How is science fiction different from fantasy?
qa.a: Sci-fi uses science to explain events; fantasy uses magic
qa.e: Sci-fi relies on real or imagined science, while fantasy relies on magic.

qa.q: A typical question that starts a sci-fi story is ___.
qa.a: 'What if people could live on the Moon?'
qa.e: Sci-fi grows from imaginative 'what if' questions about science and the future.

qa.q: Which sci-fi idea has already become real?
qa.e: Writers imagined satellites sending signals around the world, and today they do.

qa.q: The root 'tele' means ___.
qa.e: 'Tele' means far, as in telephone (sound from far) and telescope (look far).

qa.q: What does 'astronomy' study?
qa.e: 'Astro' means star, so astronomy is the study of stars and space.

qa.q: Which word means 'a written account of a person's life'?
qa.e: bio (life) + graph (write) = biography, a life story written down.

qa.q: In 'microphone', 'phone' means ___.
qa.e: 'Phone' means sound. A microphone picks up sound so that it can be made louder or recorded.

qa.q: What does 'geology' mean?
qa.a: Study of the earth and its rocks
qa.e: geo (earth) + logy (study of) = geology.

qa.q: The root 'photo' in 'photosynthesis' means ___.
qa.e: Plants use light to make food; 'photo' means light.

qa.q: 'Astronaut' comes from roots meaning ___.
qa.e: astro (star) + naut (sailor): a 'star sailor'.

qa.q: Which instrument's name means 'measure heat'?
qa.e: therm (heat) + meter (measure) = thermometer.

qa.q: Read: 'Through my glass a beetle's back / Becomes a shining shield of black.' What is the beetle's back compared to?
qa.e: The beetle's hard, shiny back is compared to a shining black shield.

qa.q: What kind of lens is a magnifying glass?
qa.e: A magnifying glass is a convex lens, thicker in the middle.

qa.q: Read: 'A leaf turns into a map of streams.' This line is an example of ___.
qa.e: It compares a leaf directly to a map, without 'like' or 'as'.

qa.q: Which word means 'to look at something carefully and in detail'?
qa.e: To examine is to look closely and carefully.

qa.q: Read: 'A drop of dew holds rainbow gleams.' What does the poet see in the dewdrop?
qa.e: 'Rainbow gleams' are flashes of rainbow colours in the dew.

qa.q: What is 'imagery' in a poem?
qa.a: Word pictures that appeal to the senses
qa.e: Imagery is language that helps us see, hear, smell, taste or feel things in our mind.

qa.q: Sita had to ___ at the tiny letters on the old coin to read them.
qa.e: To peer is to look very closely because something is hard to see.

qa.q: What is the main message of a poem about a magnifying glass?
qa.a: Looking closely reveals wonder in ordinary things
qa.e: The poem shows that careful looking makes small, everyday things amazing.

qa.q: Which is the correct spelling?
qa.e: The noun drops the 'u' from 'curious': curiosity.

qa.q: Which question word asks for a reason?
qa.e: 'Why' asks for a reason: Why is the sky blue?

qa.q: Which question is in the correct order?
qa.e: In a question, the helping verb 'does' comes before the subject 'the beetle'.

qa.q: Choose the correct question tag: 'It is raining, ___?'
qa.e: A positive statement with 'is' takes the negative tag 'isn't it?'

qa.q: Choose the correct question tag: 'You haven't seen my lens, ___?'
qa.e: A negative statement with 'haven't' takes the positive tag 'have you?'

qa.q: Which is a yes/no question?
qa.e: It begins with the helping verb 'Is' and can be answered with yes or no.

qa.q: Which word means 'eager to know or learn'?
qa.e: A curious person wants to know more.

qa.q: Choose the correct question tag: 'Meena found a snail, ___?'
qa.e: 'Found' is simple past (positive), so the tag uses 'did' in the negative: didn't she?

qa.q: Bibha Chowdhuri was a scientist in which field?
qa.e: She was a physicist who studied particles produced by cosmic rays.

qa.q: What are cosmic rays?
qa.a: High-energy particles that reach the Earth from outer space
qa.e: Cosmic rays are high-energy particles from outer space that strike the Earth's atmosphere.

qa.q: In which city was Bibha Chowdhuri born?
qa.e: She was born in Calcutta, now called Kolkata.

qa.q: With which scientist did she work at the Bose Institute?
qa.e: She worked with D. M. Bose at the Bose Institute in Kolkata.

qa.q: In which year was a star named 'Bibha' in her honour?
qa.e: The International Astronomical Union named the star 'Bibha' in 2019.

qa.q: Read: 'Bibha chose physics anyway, sat in classrooms full of young men...' What does 'anyway' show?
qa.a: She went ahead even though girls were not encouraged
qa.e: 'Anyway' shows she made her choice in spite of the difficulty mentioned before.

qa.q: Where did Bibha Chowdhuri earn her PhD?
qa.e: She earned her PhD at the University of Manchester, in Patrick Blackett's laboratory.

qa.q: The chapter title calls her 'The Beam of Light'. This is a ___.
qa.e: She is called a beam of light directly, without 'like' or 'as', because she showed the way for others. That is a metaphor.

qa.q: Who was the first woman of Indian origin to go to space?
qa.e: Kalpana Chawla flew to space in 1997 on a NASA Space Shuttle mission.

qa.q: Who is known as the 'Missile Woman of India'?
qa.e: Tessy Thomas of DRDO worked on the Agni missiles.

qa.q: Janaki Ammal was a ___.
qa.e: She was a botanist, a scientist who studies plants, and she worked on breeding better sugarcane.

qa.q: What is a pioneer?
qa.a: One of the first people to do something, opening the way for others
qa.e: A pioneer goes first and makes it easier for others to follow.

qa.q: Anna Mani is best remembered for work on ___.
qa.e: Anna Mani designed instruments to measure the weather.

qa.q: Choose the noun form: 'Her ___ to science inspired many students.'
qa.e: After 'Her' we need a noun: dedication.

qa.q: Read: 'India had to buy most weather instruments from abroad, so Anna Mani helped design and build them in India.' Which word best describes her?
qa.e: She found a practical way to solve the problem, which is what a resourceful person does.

qa.q: Kalpana Chawla was born in which state?
qa.e: Kalpana Chawla was born in Karnal, Haryana.

qa.q: Join with a relative pronoun: 'Bibha was a physicist. She studied cosmic rays.'
qa.a: Bibha was a physicist who studied cosmic rays.
qa.e: 'Who' is used for people.

qa.q: Which relative pronoun shows possession?
qa.e: 'Whose' shows that something belongs to someone: the girl whose bag is red.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'This is the microscope ___ we used in the lab.'
qa.e: A microscope is a thing, so use 'which' (or 'that').

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'Kolkata is the city ___ Bibha Chowdhuri was born.'
qa.e: 'Where' introduces a clause about a place: the city where she was born.

qa.q: Join: 'I met a scientist. Her book is about stars.'
qa.a: I met a scientist whose book is about stars.
qa.e: 'Her book' shows possession, so 'whose' replaces 'her'.

qa.q: Choose the correct option: 'The bus ___ goes to Ooty leaves at six.'
qa.e: A bus is a thing, so we use 'which' (or 'that').

qa.q: Choose the correct option: '1997 was the year ___ Kalpana Chawla first flew to space.'
qa.e: 'When' introduces a clause about a time.

qa.q: In 'The girl who won the quiz loves physics', the relative pronoun is ___.
qa.e: 'Who' joins the clause 'who won the quiz' to 'the girl'.
